 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Kedar Jha, Adv
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Chandra Bhushan Prasad, App
 =====================================================

=
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA SHEKHAR JHA  ORAL ORDER 3 03-11-2025 Heard the parties.
2. The petitioner seeks bail in connection with Simri P.S. Case No. 182 of 2012 registered for the offences under Sections 376, 341, 323, 506 and 34 of the IPC.
3. The petitioner is named in the F.I.R. and is in custody since 05.09.2024.

4. The allegation against the petitioner is to commit rape upon minor informant aged about 12 years.
5.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that present allegation raised against petitioner in the background of Mukhiya elections.

It is submitted that allegation not appears convincing out of any prudent imagination that on Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.62283 of 2025(3) dt.03-11-2025 busy road the victim was pulled to a nearby orchard and was raped.

It is submitted that considering the nature and age of informant as she claimed her age 12 years at the time of occurrence, non finding of any injury particularly when medical examination was conducted just after three hours of the occurrence creates a serious doubt qua allegation.

It is pointed out that interestingly statement of victim was not recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., therefore, her statement regarding occurrence as explained through FIR not appears of sterling quality particularly in want of her statement under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. and also in view of medical examination report as explained aforesaid.

While concluding the argument it is submitted that, petitioner is a man of clean antecedent and moreover, investigation of this case has already completed, and as Mithilesh Sahni vs The State Of Bihar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5075986/
1 such, there is no chance of tampering with the evidence.

sentences.text: 6. Learned APP appearing on behalf of the State, while opposing the prayer for bail submitted that non finding of medical injury does not lead to a conclusion ipso-facto that rape was not committed upon for the simple reason that rape is a legal finding not a medical one.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.62283 of 2025(3) dt.03-11-2025 7.

In view of aforesaid factual submission and by taking note of fact as statement of victim was not recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. qua occurrence and also upon medical examination which was conducted just after three hours of the occurrence nothing incriminating found upon, coupled with the fact as petitioner remains in custody since 05.09.2024, accordingly above named petitioner, is directed to be released on bail in connection with Simri P.S. Case No. 182 of 2012 on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned District and Additional Sessions Judge-1, Darbhanga/concerned court, subject to the conditions as mentioned under Section 480(3) of the B.N.S.S. (Chandra Shekhar Jha, J.) S.Tripathi/-
